section_summary.extract_value: This section introduces the 'be creative effect,' where instructing individuals to 'be creative' enhances the creativity of their responses in divergent thinking tasks. The present research, described as an experiment (Experiment 1), investigated this effect by measuring fluid intelligence and administering two divergent thinking tasks: one with 'be creative' instructions and another with 'be fluent' instructions. Responses were evaluated for creativity using subjective scoring and for fluency. Experiment 1 found that 'be creative' instructions led to higher quality but fewer responses, and it replicated the finding that intelligence more strongly predicts creativity when subjective ratings are used under 'be creative' instructions, compared to when creativity is scored as fluency under 'be fluent' instructions.
